alt: The Great Seal of the London Necropolis and National Mausoleum Company: a skull and crossed bones over an hourglass, within a serpent biting its tail
caption: The company’s Great Seal of 1852, with its motto Mortuis quies, vivis salus: rest for the dead, health for the living.
after: a drawing of the company’s seal

alt: Victorian engraving of a crowded dance in a chapel, with coffins and bones piled in the vault beneath the floor
caption: Enon Chapel, off the Strand, as The Poor Man’s Guardian showed it in 1847: a dance in the chapel above, coffins heaped in the vault below.
after: an engraving by an unknown artist in The Poor Man’s Guardian (1847)

alt: Watercolour of a grassy avenue and track between tall conifers and rhododendrons
caption: Railway Avenue, the trackbed of the Necropolis branch, between redwoods and rhododendrons.
author: Len Williams

alt: Watercolour of a domed classical mausoleum with a columned portico among conifers
caption: The Columbarium, built as the Earl Cadogan’s mausoleum and sold to the company in 1910. Its dome is in poor repair.
author: Jack1956

alt: Engraving of railway platforms beneath a building lettered London Necropolis Company private station
caption: The platforms of the company’s private station at 121 Westminster Bridge Road, opened in 1902.

alt: Watercolour of an ornate red brick and terracotta building front with a large arched entrance
caption: The office front of the 1902 terminus as it survives today, once the first-class entrance.
author: Davidmpye

alt: Engraving of a wrecked railway carriage on a tangle of twisted girders and rubble
caption: The Westminster Bridge Road terminus after the air raid of 16–17 April 1941, which ended the Necropolis Railway.
after: a 1941 official photograph in the US National Archives

alt: Engraving of a bronze sculpture of an angel with outstretched wings above a reclining figure, on a stone base among trees
caption: The bronze Pelham-Clinton group, Brookwood’s only Grade II* monument: a dead woman, a kneeling mourner and an angel above.
author: Jack1956

alt: Watercolour of a small pedimented mausoleum with an arcade of columns, among dark trees
caption: The Drake mausoleum, in the Lombardic manner, built for Sir William Drake around 1880–90.
author: Irid Escent

alt: Engraving of a tall Gothic shrine with a spire, behind railings
caption: The Bent memorial of about 1860, a Gothic shrine with a spirelet, one of the earliest elaborate monuments in the cemetery.
author: Tim Sheerman-Chase

alt: Engraving of an upright inscribed gravestone with a shaped top, among trees
caption: John Singer Sargent’s grave, a Portland stone stele that also commemorates his sister Emily.
author: Jack1956

alt: Engraving of a marble stele with a relief of two draped figures beneath a pediment
caption: The De Morgans’ stele. An angel reaches towards Death, who turns away holding an inverted torch; Evelyn De Morgan designed the relief.
author: Jack1956

alt: Engraving of an Egyptian-style mausoleum with a tall doorway and a winged sun on the frieze
caption: The mausoleum of Jamsetji Tata (1904), in the Egyptian manner, in the Zoroastrian ground.
author: Jack1956

alt: Watercolour of a steep-roofed chapel among trees and hedges
caption: The church of St Edward the Martyr, a former Anglican chapel, now the shrine of the saint’s relics.
author: Hassocks5489

alt: Watercolour of rows of white crosses on a lawn before a small white classical chapel
caption: The American chapel and the white marble crosses of the Brookwood American Cemetery.
author: Carcharoth

alt: Watercolour of a circular colonnaded memorial on a lawn, with autumn trees behind
caption: The Brookwood 1939–1945 Memorial, a ring of Portland stone panels, unveiled by Queen Elizabeth II in 1958.
author: Carcharoth
